page: Amazon Web Services g6.24xlarge is an accelerated computing server instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor providing 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. Hardware acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs delivering a total of 89 GB of VRAM. High-speed local scratch space includes 3,760 GB of NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct multi-core compute and inference throughput capabilities. The host achieves top 10% performance in multi-core stress-ng tests (143,501.02) and PassMark CPU encryption (95,981.04), alongside strong top 25% outcomes across Geekbench multi-core (17,481.0), PassMark CPU (76,614.46), and database operations (25,918.66). LLM inference benchmarks demonstrate top 10% prompt processing throughput across small, medium, and 70B models, reaching 12,161.03 tokens per second on 135M models and 2,838.38 tokens per second on 7B models. In contrast, single-thread Geekbench score (1,677.0) and uncached memory bandwidth fall into the middle 50% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundling of four NVIDIA L4 GPUs, 96 dedicated vCPUs, and 3,760 GB of local NVMe SSD storage yields high density for machine learning serving pipelines without requiring separate storage provisioning. However, workloads constrained strictly by per-core single-threaded frequency or unaccelerated memory write performance may find the broad core count and GPU density underutilized.

This server type is primarily matched for distributed AI model inference, medium-to-large language model serving, video and graphics rendering, multi-stream real-time transcoding, and data processing workflows requiring high local NVMe throughput alongside GPU acceleration.
